Defendant nos. 4, 13 and 18 on the other hand, claim that their predecessors took settlement of the disputed land from Gopal Chandra Sana by virtue of different registered Kabuliyats of the years 1940 and 1942. Since the settlement the lessees possessed the disputed land and their names were duly recorded in the relevant R.S. Khatian After their death the defendants have been possessing the suit land as owners by inheritance and also by purchase. Their names have also been recorded in the S.A. Khatian and they have been paying rent accordingly. These defendants have also pleaded that the suit is not maintainable. 

 9. All these grounds rest on facts, it is a settled principle that the findings of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court is binding on the High Court Division as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such, as non-consideration or misreading of material evidence affecting the Merit of the case. The judgment of the appellate court shows that in arriving at its findings the said court carefully considered all the material facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, both oral and documentary inclusive of the registered kabuliayts, R.S. and S.A. Khatians, registered sale deeds and rent receipts. The learned counsel for the petitioners could not point out any error of law in them. In the circumstances we do not find that the High Court Division, in refusing to set aside the appellate judgment, has acted illegally. No interference with the judgment of the High Court Division is therefore called for.
